questions.q: When a user clicks an IdP-initiated SSO link from inside Salesforce, what happens mechanically?
options: Salesforce redirects them to the Single Sign-On Settings page
Salesforce builds a signed SAML assertion about the current user and POSTs it directly to the SP's ACS URL
Salesforce emails the user a one-time password
Nothing; IdP-initiated links only work for Salesforce-to-Salesforce logins
questions.explain: Salesforce, acting as the IdP, builds and signs a SAML assertion for the already-authenticated user and sends it straight to the downstream SP's Assertion Consumer Service URL.

questions.q: What is the Federation ID field used for?
options: It stores the user's Salesforce password
It's a shared identifier both the IdP and SP agree represents the same person, used to match the assertion's subject to a user record
It controls which permission sets a user has
It's only used for Experience Cloud guest users
questions.explain: The Federation ID is a credential-free identifier used specifically to link a user's identity across IdP and SP, independent of login mechanics.

questions.q: Why is Federation ID often preferred over username as the SAML subject identifier?
options: Federation ID is required by the SAML specification
It carries no login credentials and can be set independently of how the user authenticates
Usernames cannot be used in SAML assertions at all
Federation ID is automatically generated and can never be changed
questions.explain: Unlike a username, the Federation ID is purely an identity-linking value with no authentication function of its own, making it a cleaner choice for the SAML subject.

questions.q: If Just-in-Time provisioning is enabled and an incoming assertion's Federation ID doesn't match any existing user, what can happen?
options: The login always fails with no side effects
Salesforce ignores the mismatch and logs the user in as a random existing user
A brand-new user record may be silently created instead of the login simply failing
The org automatically disables SSO for all users
questions.explain: With JIT provisioning configured, an unmatched Federation ID can trigger automatic creation of a new user record — useful for legitimate onboarding, but risky if the mismatch was actually a data-entry error.

questions.q: What architectural risk does the lesson highlight when a Salesforce user is deactivated but the downstream SP never receives that signal?
options: There is no risk; deactivation always propagates instantly and automatically
The downstream SP may continue trusting stale sessions or re-authentication paths after the user should have lost access
The downstream SP automatically deletes the user's account
The Federation ID is automatically cleared
questions.explain: If deactivation doesn't propagate, the downstream SP can keep trusting sessions or cached assertions for a user who should no longer have access anywhere — a direct consequence of Salesforce being the authoritative identity source.
